newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged after volatile day.

text.p: Benchmark three-month December Euroyen futures settled unchanged on Thursday after unsuccessfully trying both support and resistance in volatile trade. Late short-covering lifted the contract from lows.

Afternoon trade was led by moves in Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and the dollar, both of which were volatile in turn on comments by a senior Finance Ministry official. The key December settled at 99.05 with turnover of 89,608 contracts.

Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the Finance Ministry's International Finance bureau, told reporters Japan's monetary authorities would take decisive action against excessive foreign exchange rate moves. His comments caused Tokyo stocks to shoot higher as the yen fell sharply against the dollar.

Earlier, he was quoted as saying that Japan's interest rates are unlikely to rise anytime soon, given current economic conditions. But he was also quoted as saying he does not rule out a rise in Japanese rates in the medium term.
The first comment sparked buying of JGBs, while the second set off sales, with Euroyen futures dragged around in tandem.
"The market currently has little of real substance to trade on, so it is vulnerable to being knocked around in this way by comments," a trader at a city bank said.

December dipped as low as 98.99 in mid-afternoon. A trader at a trust bank said people who still believed interest rates may rise in the latter half of the year had apparently taken out short positions they were forced to cover, and were joined by others who had sold short this morning.
While the Nikkei did close up by 274.53 at 20,564.46, its failure to rise even more also gave operators an excuse for short-covering of the December, the trust bank trader said.

Given a lack of other factors ahead of next week's Group of Seven summit and the release of the Bank of Japan's tankan survey on June 25, the market is keenly watching the dollar, traders said. The dollar fluctuated wildly from 111.17 to 115.80 yen in Asia and was clinging near 114 yen by late Tokyo.

Unless the dollar breaks below 110 yen, and barring any other strong factors, the key December is unlikely to rise much above 99.08, a trader at a city bank said. But sharp slides are unlikely unless the greenback breaks decisively above 116 yen, and may well be limited even then. "After all, today the dollar went to 115.80 yen and support held at 98.99," he added.

Although some traders predicted quiet trade for Friday, others thought this unlikely and added that there was market talk that Japan's first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data, due out on Friday at 0630 GMT, may be strong.
"In this case, if both stocks and the dollar are strong, we could see sales of the key December that might take it down below 98.95," the trust bank trader said.

In the interbank market, overnight call money was being traded at around 0.46 percent in the afternoon against 0.47 percent on Wednesday as fund-raising needs tapered off ahead of the end of the bank reporting period on Friday, traders said.

There was also some talk that Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, whose fund-raising helped push rates up earlier this week, may have taken too much in the way of funds, forcing it to become a supplier to the market and keeping the overnight rate down.

Around 10 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.59 percent. Another 10 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued at 0.58 percent along with 100 billion yen of one-month at 0.57 percent.
TIFFE said trade in Euroyen futures and options would start at 0045 GMT (0845 JST) on June 25 in connection with the release of the tankan. -- Elaine Lies, Tokyo Treasury Desk
